script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Hunger Within

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

We open on a close-up of a STOVE, the burners flickering to life as JANE (mid 30s, determined) pours herself a cup of coffee. She sits at the kitchen table, flipping through a well-worn cookbook.

JANE
(to herself)
This is it. The big day. I can do this.

She closes the cookbook and rises, wiping her hands on her apron.

INT. RESTAURANT - DAY

Jane stands behind the counter of her new restaurant, THE HUNGRY CHEF. Customers mill about, chatting with each other and the staff. JANE's ex-husband, MIKE (mid 40s, bitter), watches from the corner.

MIKE
(spitting out a mouthful of coffee)
You think you're better than me? Opening up this fancy-schmancy restaurant?

JANE
(smiling)
I'm just following my dream, Mike. I always knew I could do more than work the factory line.

MIKE
(scoffing)
And look how that's working out for you.

Jane ignores him, greeting customers and taking orders.

INT. OFFICE - DAY

Jane sits at her desk, pouring over financial reports and menus. SARAH (late 20s, eager) enters, a stack of flyers in hand.

SARAH
Jane, these are ready to go! I printed up a hundred for the farmers market this weekend.

JANE
Great work, Sarah. Let's make sure every penny counts.

INT. KITCHEN - EVENING

Jane stands in front of the oven, checking on a roast. The kitchen is in chaos, with staff rushing about. MIKE enters, covered in grease.

MIKE
(mockingly)
Need some help?

JANE
(tired but calm)
I've got it, Mike. But thank you for offering.

INT. DINING ROOM - NIGHT

Customers fill the dining room, laughing and chatting. Jane makes her rounds, ensuring everything is running smoothly. She notices a FAMILY huddled in a corner, clearly struggling to pay their bill.

JANE
(approaching)
May I help you with something?

FATHER
(embarrassed)
No, no. We'll manage.

JANE
(smiling)
I insist. Here, take this and come back another time when things are better for you.

She hands them a voucher for a free meal. The family is grateful, and Jane watches them leave with a smile.

INT. OFFICE - NIGHT

Jane sits at her desk, exhausted but satisfied. She calls her MOTHER on the phone.

JANE
(voice shaking)
Mom, I did it. I really did it.

MOTHER
(tearfully)
I'm so proud of you, Jane. Keep reaching for the stars.

INT. RESTAURANT - NIGHT

The restaurant is emptying out, and Jane locks up for the night. MIKE waits for her outside.

MIKE
You can't keep running from me, Jane.

JANE
(firm)
I'm not running. I'm living.

MIKE
(laughing)
Good luck with that.

JANE walks away, leaving Mike behind.

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

Jane brews a cup of coffee, her face reflecting in the steamy mug.

JANE
(to herself)
Another day, another dream.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
